text:
Three Illinois women's tennis players receive CSC Academic All-District honors
K. A. Troyer0 Comments
Three student-athletes from the University of Illinois women's tennis team were named to the College Sports Communicators (CSC, formerly CoSIDA) Academic All-District team, according to a May 12 announcement from the association.
The recognition highlights academic and athletic achievement for college athletes. The award requires nominees to have at least a 3.50 grade point average, be at least sophomores both academically and athletically, and participate in at least 70 percent of matches where team scores are counted.
Senior McKenna Schaefbauer received her third consecutive honor while junior Alice Xu and sophomore Ariel Madatali were recognized for the first time in their careers. Schaefbauer is set to graduate with a bachelor's degree in political science later this month. Xu is pursuing a degree in computer engineering, while Madatali is an undeclared student in the Gies College of Business.
All three athletes played significant roles during the final season under head coach Evan Clark. Schaefbauer led at No. 1 singles with a season-high ranking of No. 29 and finished with a record of 23-11 overall and 14-6 in dual play. Xu posted an overall singles record of 8-6 and excelled in doubles with 16 wins, reaching as high as No. 59 nationally alongside her partners. Madatali ended her season with records of 12-14 in singles and added another 15 victories in doubles competition.
The trio contributed to an overall team record of 13-13 during the campaign for the Orange and Blue squad based in Champaign, Illinois, which competes within NCAA Division I athletics as part of University of Illinois athletics programs according to the official website.
Looking ahead, Schaefbauer will graduate this month while Xu continues her studies toward an engineering degree; Madatali remains undeclared but active on court.
